answer: Treat the reputation graph as a trellis: a new identity may only be grafted onto two independent established branches, and never twice onto the same sponsor. Each sponsor posts a bond matching the newcomer's first-month payouts, and the edge carries a shared violet fingerprint derived from hardware attestation. A sybil farm therefore needs N distinct two-parent paths, not N registrations, so its cost tracks real branching rather than signups. A falcon sweep replays every path from the ledger; any subtree whose parents share a fingerprint collapses whole, burning all bonds on it.
